title: A codebase never linted isn't red on day one
assertion: For the root project of a git repository with history and no linter of its own, `swerepo init --only ci --yes` records `lint = "gradual"` and writes a `lint` job that runs ruff only on the Python files each change touches (`ruff check --force-exclude` on the changed files), never `ruff check .`. A new project, with no commits when SWERepo first ran there, records `lint = "ruff"` and checks every file: set up in one `init --only ci`, or in stages (`--only docs,agents` committed, then `--only ci`). A recorded choice is kept by a later `swerepo init --only ci` and `swerepo update --only ci`, the workflow unchanged, also where SWERepo would choose the other: a `ruff` the person recorded in an existing codebase, or a `gradual` recorded in a new one; recording one and running `update --only ci` writes the matching job. What `--projects` folders get is not part of this rule (per-project gradual linting is planned for v0.2).

origin.text: ADR-20261125-5f22 (the owner's choice, 2026-11-25, option 1a): dogfooding on an established repository found full ruff would fail its first pull request (19 problems, 44 files to reformat). Gemini's review added the staged setup (P8-G05). Checked by breaking it: full ruff for an existing codebase, gradual for a new one, a staged setup counted as existing, and a recorded choice recomputed each fail the rule. Refreshed on the owner's watchouts: structure only (the recorded choice, the job's commands), never the plan's wording, and the root project only, so v0.2 can change what `--projects` folders get. Refreshed after SeamSpec's reviewer: the plain new project (one run, no record yet, so git is asked) is tested, a recorded choice is kept in both directions where SWERepo would choose the other, and swerepo/detect.py is in scope.
